elements.texte:
[cheerful] The sales team wants to split its advisors between the cities.

The more customers a city has, the more advisors it gets.

So it needs the number of customers in each city.

Everything starts from the customers table, which holds one row per customer.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Group by city groups the customers by city.

The 10 customers form 6 groups, one for each city.

Count star then counts the customers in each group.

Each group becomes one row of the result: 6 rows in all.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Count isn’t the only calculation you can do on a group.

Sum adds up the values, and A-V-G gives their average.

Min and max keep the smallest and the largest value.

With A-V-G of age, each city gets the average age of its customers.

In Lyon, Lucas Bernard is 28 and Hugo Laurent is 52: the average is 40.
